audits.title: 394 Gentamicin Guidelines – Available but Are They Followed? a Retrospective Audit
audits.standard: Trust gentamicin prescribing protocol (dose adjustment for age, renal function and weight; level monitoring)

cycle1.result: 2224 doses; dosing not adjusted for obesity or creatinine clearance (p<0.05); 86% needing a level had one, 15% taken too early; 100% with level >1 had next dose held.

audits.citation: Ash J, Wolff N. 394 Gentamicin Guidelines – Available but Are They Followed? a Retrospective Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac039.270.

audits.title: P26 An audit of the use of amikacin for early onset sepsis in premature neonates in an inpatient neonatal unit
audits.standard: Trust Neonatal Infection Guideline: 100% adherence to criteria, amikacin 15 mg/kg, level at 24 hours before second dose, further doses only if level <5 mg/L or on pharmacist advice
audits.setting: Two neonatal units in one Trust

cycle1.result: 100% adhered to guideline criteria and 100% prescribed 15 mg/kg; 12 (24%) had no level at 24 hours; of 38 with 24-hour levels only 6 (16%) were <5 mg/L; 17/23 (74%) in range at 36 hours; 2 patients received doses despite levels >5 mg/L.

audits.intervention: Recommended change from 24-hourly to 36-hourly dosing; re-audit planned in one year.
audits.other_findings: No direct correlation seen between gestational age, severity of illness and amikacin levels.
audits.citation: Caroline D, Tami B, Lidia T, Ioana G. P26 An audit of the use of amikacin for early onset sepsis in premature neonates in an inpatient neonatal unit. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2018;103(2):e1.31-e1. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2017-314584.37.

audits.title: Quality assurance of data collection in an aminoglycoside dosing service.
audits.standard: Complete documentation of data needed to interpret serum aminoglycoside levels
audits.setting: Aminoglycoside dosing service, Royal Columbian Hospital

cycle1.result: Complete documentation in 75% of pre-dose and 63% of post-dose levels.

audits.intervention: Education via Pharmacy Bulletin, revision of Laboratory and IV Medication Manuals, communication with head nurses and active pharmacist follow-up of missing information.

cycle2.result: Complete documentation 93% for pre-dose and 84% for post-dose levels (p < 0.001).

audits.other_findings: Problems included unawareness of form procedures and inaccurate assumptions of infusion times.
audits.citation: Lew KH, Malyuk DL. Quality assurance of data collection in an aminoglycoside dosing service. Can J Hosp Pharm. 1991;44(5):239-243. PMID: 10115577.

audits.title: A prospective laboratory-based audit of gentamicin use and therapeutic monitoring.
audits.standard: Therapeutic serum gentamicin levels (peak above 5 mg/L; trough below 2 mg/L)

cycle1.result: First monitored peaks were subtherapeutic in 58 (78%) courses; initial troughs above 2 mg/L in nine (12%).

audits.other_findings: 73% received 80 mg three times daily; authors recommend weight-based dosing in no more than two daily doses.
audits.citation: Saunders NJ, Adams DJ, Lynn WA. A prospective laboratory-based audit of gentamicin use and therapeutic monitoring. J Antimicrob Chemother. 1995;36(4):729-736. doi:10.1093/jac/36.4.729. PMID: 8591950.

audits.title: (ID: 54) Transforming gentamicin prescribing: an audit on safety and compliance
audits.standard: Local TDM guideline (Urban & Craig nomogram): 90% correct dose ±10%; 90% levels at correct time; 90% levels correctly interpreted and redosed
audits.setting: Four hospitals, University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Correct dose 61.2% (82/134); levels at the right time 44% (59/134); correct redosing 41.6% (32/77).

audits.intervention: Gentamicin calculator, ward education, maximum dose warning and aligned pathology warning flag.
audits.other_findings: 8.2% dosed without weight and 7.5% without height; correct dosing ranged 52.6% to 77.8% by site.
audits.citation: Abusikken A, Hendrick A, Harley J, Roche N. (ID: 54) Transforming gentamicin prescribing: an audit on safety and compliance. International Journal of Pharmacy Practice. 2025;33(Supplement_1):i23-i24. doi:10.1093/ijpp/riaf093.029.
